propositions: Store transaction kernel recommendation conflates two-writer architecture with local components that already share locks and canonical mechanics; proposed cross-writer kernel would likely become a god object absorbing materially different reconciler semantics with unproven benefit over fault-injection testing.

Reconciler typed cutover should focus on representation cleanup and discriminated unions (not completing ADR 0103) but carries high migration risk from local-ID/Jira-key and exception-shape regressions; benefits only materialize after bridges are deleted.

Burr workflow engine adoption requires spike testing through existing Runner/Recorder seams with crash-before/after-effect matrix coverage; current framework parallelism is experimental and typed-state unsupported; custom interpreter remains valid third option pending evidence.

Runner lifecycle function-size gate should add shrink-only baseline with explicit LOC/NLOC semantics and extract lifecycle helpers while preserving intentional telemetry/finalization invariants; this is high-confidence near-term win with behavior-preserving test coverage.

Attestation versioning should defer inner-manifest v2 to the first incompatible semantic change; doing it now adds maintenance risk without removing current HMAC/opcert v1 ambiguity; opcert v1 already uses DSSE-PAE, in-toto Statement v1, and versioned predicates.

OperationSnapshot authority promotion should proceed surface-by-surface with consumer-level metamorphic tests and schema extension rather than generation; configuration ownership is already enforced; long-term benefit is high with measured parity gates.
